newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso softer on pre-weekend dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso softer on pre-weekend dollar demand.

text.p: Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had reversed early firmness and were softer at mid-morning Thursday on pre-weekend demand for dollars, traders said.
"The market is very calm and dollars were even on offer despite month-end pressures," a trader said. "Nonetheless, 48-hour contracts are softer as they do not need to be settled until Monday."
Traders said demand for dollars at 48 hours often increases on Thursdays, as they may be paid for the following Monday in pesos, which can meanwhile be invested in the money market.
The 48-hour peso stood 0.2 centavo weaker at 7.8430/7.8470 per dollar, while its 24-hour counterpart was 0.5 centavo firmer at 7.8310/7.8360 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed 0.9 centavo firmer at 7.8230/7.8270 per dollar.
